norms.definition: Create things or changes that others have reason to value; uptake by an independent counterparty is evidence, internal applause is a hypothesis.
Make commitments answerable to evidence and preserve the ability to discover that they were wrong; a changed criterion does not rewrite what was promised.
Steward the resources and capabilities that make future worthwhile choices possible; spending for an enduring capability can be good stewardship, maintaining a dead institution is not.
Do not finance the factory's advantage by imposing unconsented costs on outsiders.

Measurements are defeasible evidence of the values, not substitutes for them. A favorable measurement is insufficient when supported consequences contradict the value it represents. Missing measurement alone is not evidence of failure.

reasons: The charter's norms and cards form a coherent, measurable set covering epistemic integrity, consequence, cost discipline, and fidelity with reasonable thresholds.

The charter's own text already lists seven cards, including independent-uptake and well-formed-floor, while the submitted edition 1 carries only six and drops independent-uptake; adopting it whole would silently enact a different card set than the one the world input presents, so the discrepancy should be resolved before the edition is adopted.
The charter’s unresolved-commitment card uses a forecast window although that observation’s unresolved-share measurement is not meaningfully forecast-based, risking an invalid preflight.
The forecast-skill card requires a nonnegative skill floor, but skill is defined as forecast Brier minus baseline Brier, so positive values indicate worse forecasts.
The proposed cards are internally inconsistent with edition 1: independent-uptake is absent, and unresolved commitments are specified separately despite the existing censorship-bound card.
